absent: Full layouts of wait options, task, signal, sighand, pid, pid namespace, coverage, filter and namespace proxy beyond fields touched here.
Lock order and interrupt context among task-list, sighand, pid-map, coverage, affinity and RCU protection.
Semantics of wait consideration, parent notification, autoreap, pidfd notification and orphaned-group handling.
Fallback reaper choice and live-thread tests beyond their call sites.
Trace attach, trap delivery, stop state machine and credential rules beyond unlink and detach.
Group-exit, coredump rendezvous, exec notification and thread-group change guards end to end.
Complete termination teardown order guarantees and failure handling for each exit helper.
Numeric values of signals, wait flags, pid types, exit states, job-control bits, stack sizes and histogram limits.
Remote coverage map lifecycle, sequence use and area management outside task exit.
Filter-tree sharing, orphan wakeup protocol and program lifetime outside release.

findings.text: Pid helpers supply reference held pid handles from a task and type or from a numeric identifier in the caller namespace, plus a direct lookup of a numeric identifier in the active namespace of current.

Pid lookup holds RCU read protection while dereferencing task pid storage or namespace state and acquiring a reference, then releases it. Disabling pid allocation serializes clearing of the adding mark in the namespace under the pid map spin lock.

A wait target counts as effectively a child when current is the relevant parent, or when thread-group waiting is permitted and current shares a thread group with that parent. Plain waits consult the real parent while traced waits consult the ptrace parent.

Traced waiting scans the traced list and reports the first considerable task. Identified waiting first considers the thread-group identifier as untraced and then, when the thread identifier names a traced task, considers it as traced, otherwise reports no status.

Reaper selection prefers a live thread inside the exiting father, else the closest ancestor marked as child subreaper that stays at the same pid namespace level and has a live thread, stopping before the root task, else a supplied fallback reaper.

Exiting tasks reparent children, become zombie, notify the appropriate parent, and move to dead with deferred release when autoreaped. Leaders notify only with an empty thread group, untraced non-leaders autoreap after pidfd handling, and a pending multithread exec waiter is awakened.

Reparenting first releases traced children, chooses a new reaper, retargets each thread real parent to it while restoring the normal parent when untraced, emits configured parent-death signals, normalizes the exit signal, opportunistically reaps empty zombie groups, handles orphaned groups, then transfers the children list.

Trace unlink requires existing trace state, clears syscall tracing and emulation work, restores parent linkage from the real parent, drops the stored tracer credential, zeroes trace state under the sighand lock, clears trap state, re-arms stop pending when a group stop remains and the task is not exiting, and wakes the child when stop or traced sleep is pending.

Tracer exit walks tracees safely, requests forced termination for those marked exit-kill, detaches each, and collects newly dead ones. Detach of a zombie leader with an empty group either notifies an outside parent or, for same-group parents that ignore children or autoreap, wakes the parent and marks dead.

The sighand lock with interrupts controlled protects trace flags and job control during unlink, child disposition checks, group-exit and coredump rendezvous, seccomp detach, and the exiting mark plus pending queue drain.
Child avoidance holds when the child signal disposition is ignore or the no-wait flag is set, evaluated while holding the sighand lock.

Unused kernel stack is estimated by scanning from the stack end across zeroed canary words in a growth-dependent direction and measuring the distance. A check bins used size into a histogram and records a new low-water free mark under a dedicated lock with an informational message, and is compiled out in one configuration.

Kernel stack accounting updates per-page counters for virtual-mapped stacks by iterating all pages or updates one node-local counter for contiguous stacks. The exit path also drops memory-cgroup charges for virtual-mapped stack pages.

Task exit clears local and remote coverage associations when present, requires consistent ownership and non-remote use of the local slot, resets task mode and area and sequence, advances object sequence, removes matching remote map entries, and frees area and object when the last reference drops.
Kernel-thread exit records the supplied result, and when affinity membership exists removes it under the affinity mutex before freeing any preferred mask.

Namespace teardown replaces the task proxy with null. A non-null replacement gains an active reference first, the swap occurs under the task lock after a sleepable-context check, and the old proxy is released afterwards.

Filter release applies only to exiting tasks with an attached filter, detaches under the sighand lock, then walks the predecessor chain to wake poll waiters whose user count reaches zero and to destroy programs and containers whose reference count reaches zero.

Signal exit marks exiting under a thread-group change guard, drains the private pending set and list to a local list for later flush, retargets shared pending signals while work remains outside group exit, consumes stop pending toward group-stop completion, and after unlocking notifies the group-leader real parent when this task completed the stop.

Process termination is a non-returning entry that coordinates group and coredump state, tracing hooks, ordered resource teardown, last-thread handling with init protection and accounting, zombie notification with connector and policy release, and final scheduler and RCU handoff to the dead state with lock and stack checks.

Exit of the last thread of global init panics with the group or supplied code. Coredump participation is serialized with group-exit flag updates while holding the sighand lock and marking post-dump before handling outside the lock.

Observed state includes task linkage and tracing membership, exit state and code and signal, parent pointers, children and traced lists, signal and sighand pointers, job control and flags, blocked and pending sets, stack and coverage and namespace and seccomp and affinity members; signal state carries group exit code and flags, stop counts, subreaper marks and core and exec rendezvous; wait options carry target identifier and flags; namespaces carry allocation marks; coverage objects carry owner, mode, sequence, remote sizing, lock and refcount; filters carry predecessor, program, wait queue and user and reference counts.

Behavior depends on externally defined constants for signals and dispositions, wait options, pid types, exit states, tracing and job-control and group-stop flags, and stack sizes and event thresholds, whose numeric values are not shown here.

Tracer teardown can request termination of marked tracees and can convert zombies to dead with parent wakeups, so callers hold task-list protection during notification decisions and defer final release to a list processed after unlocking.

Reparenting and zombie transition hold the task-list write lock with interrupts disabled across reaper selection, list transfer and notification decisions. Signal-exit stop completion uses the task-list read lock for parent notification.
